'''Jean-Michel Muller''' (born 1961) is a French mathematician and computer scientist working in the field of [[computer arithmetic]]. 

He is known for his early work on online arithmetic, in particular the [[BKM algorithm]], for his influential work on the correct rounding of elementary functions, in particular on the [[Rounding#Table-maker's dilemma|Table Maker's Dilemma]], and for having authored two reference textbooks: <em>Elementary Functions: algorithms and implementation</em><ref name="Muller_2016">{{cite book |last=Muller |first=Jean-Michel |date= |title=Elementary Functions: algorithms and implementation |edition=3rd |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4899-7983-4 |location= |publisher=Springer |page= |isbn=978-1-4899-7981-0 |access-date=}}</ref> (first edition in 1997) and the  <em>Handbook of Floating Point Arithmetic</em><ref name="Muller_2018">{{cite book |last1=Muller |first1=Jean-Michel |last2=Brunie |first2=Nicolas | last3=de Dinechin |first3=Florent | last4=Jeannerod | first4=Claude-Pierre | last5=Joldes |first5=Mioara | last6=Lefèvre |first6=Vincent |last7=Melquiond |first7=Guillaume |last8=Revol |first8=Nathalie|author8-link=Nathalie Revol |last9=Torres |first9=Serge |title=Handbook of Floating-Point Arithmetic |date=2018 |publisher=[[Birkhäuser]] |edition=2nd | isbn=978-3-319-76525-9 <!-- print --> |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-76526-6 |url=}}</ref> (first edition in 2010).

==Education and career==
Born in 1961, Jean-Michel Muller holds an engineering degree from [[École nationale supérieure d'informatique et de mathématiques appliquées de Grenoble|ENSIMAG]]. He defended his PhD <em>Methodologies for Calculating Elementary Functions</em> in 1985 at the [[Institut National Polytechnique de Grenoble]]. He is currently a [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] Research Director at [[École normale supérieure de Lyon#Sciences|LIP]], the computer science laboratory at [[École normale supérieure de Lyon|Ecole Normale Supérieure de Lyon]]. He was head of the LIP between 2001 and 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jean-Michel Muller, spécialiste de l’arithmétique des ordinateurs, LIP |url=https://www.ens-lyon.fr/recherche/panorama-de-la-recherche/prix-et-distinctions/jean-michel-muller-specialiste-de |access-date=2025-10-02}}</ref>

He obtained a CNRS Bronze Medal in 1990, the 2nd Seymour Cray France award in 1991,  the CNRS Silver Medal in 2013<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jean-Michel Muller|url=https://www.cnrs.fr/fr/personne/jean-michel-muller|access-date=2025-10-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Gaudel |first=Marie-Claude |date=2014 |title=Jean-Michel Muller, médaille d'argent 2013 du CNRS |url=https://1024.socinfo.fr/2014/01/1024_2_2014_165.pdf |access-date=2025-10-02 |work=1024 – Bulletin de la société informatique de France}}</ref> and the Prix [[La Recherche]] in 2013.<ref> {{cite web |title=Palmarès 2013 – Le Prix La Recherche |url=http://www.leprixlarecherche.com/palmares-2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170630061125/http://www.leprixlarecherche.com/palmares-2013 |archive-date=2017-06-30 |language=fr}}</ref> He became an [[List of fellows of IEEE Computer Society|IEEE Fellow]] in 2017.   He was awarded the Grand Prix Inria - Académie des sciences in 2025. 



== Involvement in the computer arithmetic community ==
Jean-Michel Muller has been very active in the development and animation of the computer arithmetic community: in France he created and lead a team of mathematicians and computer scientists, with the vision of gathering all aspects of computer arithmetic, from hardware to software and formal proofs. Internationally, he has been general chair of the [[ARITH Symposium on Computer Arithmetic|ARITH International Symposium on Computer Arithmetic]] in 1991, in 1999, and in 2015, and general chair of the [[:simple:International_Symposium_on_Scientific_Computing,_Computer_Arithmetic,_and_Validated_Numerics|International Symposium on Scientific Computing, Computer Arithmetic, and Validated Numerics]] in 1997. He also served on the ARITH steering committee board.
